How do heating method and temperature affect your experience?

Heating method and temperature control are two of the most consequential decisions a cannabis consumer makes when selecting a vaporizer. Choosing the wrong combination means losing flavor, wasting potency, and missing the full terpene profile a product offers.

What is the difference between convection and conduction heating?

Convection heating circulates hot air around the cannabis material rather than pressing it against a heated surface. Conduction heating places the material in direct contact with a heated element. Convection tends to deliver cleaner, more even flavor because the plant material heats gradually and uniformly. Conduction heats faster but risks uneven results and can degrade delicate terpenes at the point of contact.

Why does temperature control matter for potency and terpenes?

Temperature control directly determines which cannabinoids and terpenes reach the consumer. Different compounds activate at different heat levels, so precise settings preserve both potency and aromatic complexity. Running a device too hot destroys terpenes before they can be inhaled; running it too cool leaves active compounds unvaporized.
